results.basis: SELF-DECLARED: RESEARCHED 2026-10-24 (housing lane 0a, the NHPI national-accounts lead). Statistics Canada's own 'User Guide: Canadian System of Macroeconomic Accounts' (Catalogue 13-606-G), section 7.4.2 'Income and expenditure accounts deflation', says the GDP-by-expenditure table of the income and expenditure accounts (this node, IMDB record 1901) is deflated mostly by price indexes, and its Table 7.1 'Level of detail in the compilation of real GDP' gives 'NHPI, MLS' as the 'Main deflator source' for residential structures investment expenditure. The table's footnote expands it: "NHPI = new housing price index". A methodology table cell naming a source grades as a caption (PLAYBOOK-CORPUS 7a). The guide's chapters date from 2016, some updated 22 February 2021; it is still the current edition on Statistics Canada's site. The 'MLS' in the same cell is NOT wired: the footnote calls it the 'multiple listing service price index', which is not the title of CREA's MLS Home Price Index (crea-mls-hpi). Read live from the cited PDF (HTTP 200), quote verbatim from the table row.

targetReport.title: New Housing Price Index (NHPI)
targetReport.description: Statistics Canada's monthly index of contractors' selling prices for new single, semi-detached and row houses, with the same detailed specifications over time, in 27 census metropolitan areas (December 2016 = 100). Its weights come from CMHC's Market Absorption Survey. It feeds the CPI's homeowners' replacement-cost and mortgage-interest components, and the national accounts use it to deflate the housing stock. The url is StatCan's survey description (IMDB) page, not an edition page. Minted 2026-10-17.
